newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Q1 retailers' profits down from Q4 pace.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Q1 retailers' profits down from Q4 pace.

text.p: After-tax profits of U.S. retailers fell to 1.5 cents per dollar of sales in the first quarter of 1997 from a revised 2.3 cents per sales dollar in the fourth quarter of last year, the Commerce Department said on Wednesday.
By comparison, a year earlier, in the first quarter of 1996, retailers earned profits after taxes of 1.3 cents per dollar of sales.
Previously the department reported that fourth-quarter profits were 2.4 cents per sales dollar but it revised that down slightly.
Retailers generated total after-tax profits in the first quarter of $3.68 billion, down from $6.37 billion in the fourth quarter but up from $2.94 billion a year earlier in the first quarter of 1996.
The Commerce Department based its findings on quarterly financial reports supplied by 545 corporations.
Retailers had total sales in the first quarter of $238.54 billion, down from $271.93 billion in the fourth quarter but up from $227.57 billion in the first quarter of 1996, the department said.
The after-tax figures are for retailers with assets of $50 million or more and are not seasonally adjusted.
